work.intro1: Production platforms I helped build with cross-functional delivery teams —
work.introEmph: what each one does, what I contributed, and the stack I worked in.

miite.name: Make it in the Emirates — Awards Platform
miite.blurb: Public-facing awards platform for the UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology's Make it in the Emirates program, serving applicants, jurors, and program operators. I contributed across the backend, data layer, and AWS delivery pipeline.

caseStudy.role: Full-Stack Software Engineer · cross-functional delivery team
caseStudy.overview: The UAE Ministry of Industry & Advanced Technology needed a public-facing platform to run the Make it in the Emirates Awards, with separate flows for applicants, jurors, and program operators. It had to meet government security and availability requirements at 5,000+ concurrent users.
caseStudy.system: Next.js frontend and NestJS backend over PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM, deployed on AWS (VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, Secrets Manager). Container-first pipelines ship Docker images through ECR to ECS via CodeBuild and CodePipeline. Server-side rendering for SEO; Jest, Vitest, and React Testing Library suites gate each release; structured logging and monitoring run in CloudWatch.
caseStudy.contributions: Developed domain-driven NestJS modules and Next.js features for the applicant, juror, and operator flows alongside the frontend and backend teams. · Designed and tuned PostgreSQL schemas with Prisma, adding targeted indexes and query optimizations that cut API latency by ~35% under production load. · Implemented JWT authentication, role-based access control, and structured DTO validation across the API surface with the backend team. · Helped move delivery to container-first CI/CD, reducing deployment time from ~20 minutes to under 5. · Added CloudWatch monitoring and structured logging to the services I worked on, and maintained Jest, Vitest, and RTL coverage.

servicesMarketplace.name: Services Marketplace — API-first Backend
servicesMarketplace.blurb: API-first services marketplace backend connecting clients with lawyers through a request-and-bid workflow, with escalation handling, in-app payments through a Paymob wallet, and live chat. I built the Laravel backend and the Filament admin panel with the product engineering team.

caseStudy.overview: Clients needed a structured way to find the right lawyer and agree on a price, and firms needed a backend to receive, bid on, and manage cases. The platform runs a request-and-bid marketplace with payments, real-time chat, voice and SMS, and escalation handling in a single bilingual (EN/AR) product.
caseStudy.system: API-first Laravel backend with Sanctum authentication, attribute-based routing, and self-validating DTOs, administered through a role-based Filament (Livewire) panel. MySQL for relational data and Redis for cache and queues. Laravel Reverb WebSockets for chat, Twilio for voice and SMS, Firebase Cloud Messaging for mobile push, S3 for media, and Paymob for the in-app wallet, payments, and withdrawals. Pest and PHPUnit cover the domain logic.
caseStudy.contributions: Implemented the request-and-bid workflow connecting clients with lawyers, including escalation handling, as transactional Laravel services. · Built the in-app wallet integration with Paymob for payments, payouts, and withdrawals. · Designed self-validating DTOs and attribute-based routing under Sanctum authentication with the backend team. · Implemented parts of the real-time and messaging layer with the feature team: Laravel Reverb WebSocket chat, Twilio voice and SMS, FCM push, and S3 media storage. · Built the role-based Filament (Livewire) admin panel, contributed to the EN/AR localization, and wrote Pest / PHPUnit tests for the workflows above.

sabeel.name: Sabeel — Mobile Backend
sabeel.blurb: Laravel API and AWS infrastructure behind Sabeel, a mobile app with thousands of active users. I contributed to the data layer, API hardening, and production infrastructure alongside the backend and DevOps teams.

caseStudy.role: Backend Engineer · backend and DevOps teams
caseStudy.overview: Sabeel, a growing mobile app with thousands of active users, needed a backend that held latency steady under load, plus a deployment pipeline and monitoring the team could rely on.
caseStudy.system: Laravel REST API on AWS ECS behind an Application Load Balancer, MySQL on Amazon RDS, and static assets on S3 + CloudFront. Deploys run as containers through ECR, CodeBuild, and CodePipeline; secrets live in Secrets Manager, access is IAM-scoped, and CloudWatch carries the alarms.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed normalized relational data models and optimized complex SQL queries, reducing API latency under production load. · Implemented authentication flows and request validation across the API with the backend team. · Provisioned and maintained production AWS infrastructure with the DevOps team: EC2, RDS, S3, IAM, and Secrets Manager. · Set up CloudWatch dashboards and alarms for the API and database tier so the team had a shared view of production regressions.

esl.name: Egyptian Schools League — Competition Engine
esl.blurb: Platform that runs the Egyptian Schools League, a national inter-school sports competition: team onboarding, results entry, rule-based scoring, rankings, and live leaderboards. I built the NestJS rules engine and the Next.js operator dashboards and onboarding screens with the delivery team.

caseStudy.role: Full-Stack Software Engineer · cross-functional delivery team
caseStudy.overview: Operators were running the league's competitions out of spreadsheets: slow scoring, fragile state, and no real-time visibility for participants. The platform replaces that with structured team onboarding and results entry, a configurable rules engine, and live leaderboards.
caseStudy.system: Next.js frontend and NestJS backend with a modular rules engine, PostgreSQL via Prisma ORM, WebSockets for live leaderboard updates, and a Docker-based deployment.
caseStudy.contributions: Built the NestJS rules engine for competition scoring and ranking on Prisma/PostgreSQL with the backend team. · Built the live WebSocket leaderboard pipeline and the Next.js operator dashboards that consume it. · Contributed onboarding and results-entry screens to the team's shared, responsive component set, replacing spreadsheet workflows with structured forms and validation.

whatsappBot.name: WhatsApp AI Chatbot Automation
whatsappBot.blurb: Serverless chatbot on AWS Lambda and Amazon Lex, reached over WhatsApp through Twilio, that answers routine support inquiries and hands off to a human agent when confidence drops. I designed and built the Python orchestration and the Lex intent model, drawing on the support team's ticket history.

caseStudy.role: Software Engineer · independent delivery for the customer-support team
caseStudy.overview: Support agents were handling repetitive inquiries by hand: order status, opening hours, common FAQs. The team needed an automated first line of response that answers instantly and escalates cleanly to a human.
caseStudy.system: Event-driven pipeline: Twilio webhook → AWS Lambda (Python) → Amazon Lex for intent recognition and slot filling, with credentials in AWS Secrets Manager and CloudWatch for tracing. Scales to zero between conversations.
caseStudy.contributions: Designed the intent and slot taxonomy from the support team's ticket history. · Wrote the Python Lambda orchestration bridging Lex, Twilio, and the internal support tooling, with secrets in Secrets Manager and CloudWatch logging. · Automated the common request types, with hand-off to a human agent when confidence dropped, cutting manual triage for the support team.

altanfeethi.name: Altanfeethi — Azure Delivery
altanfeethi.blurb: Azure infrastructure, API gateway, and release pipelines for Altanfeethi's client-facing application. I independently provisioned the Azure infrastructure, configured API Management as the API gateway, and set up the release pipelines.

caseStudy.overview: Altanfeethi's client-facing application needed Azure infrastructure in place, an API gateway fronting its services, and a release process the team could trust before going to production.
caseStudy.system: Azure compute and storage, Azure API Management fronting the service surface, and release pipelines through Azure DevOps with environment gates.
caseStudy.contributions: Provisioned the Azure infrastructure layout — subscriptions, networking, identity, and policy. · Configured Azure API Management: routing, throttling, and key management for the platform's APIs. · Set up the release pipelines and environment gates that moved the application from staging to production.

r1.summary: Challenge Group is an AWS/Huawei Cloud partner delivering government and enterprise platforms across Egypt, KSA, and the UAE. Contributed to multiple production platforms as part of cross-functional Agile delivery teams.
r1.b1: Develop NestJS and Laravel backend services for platforms with 5,000+ concurrent users, on PostgreSQL/Prisma and MySQL. Targeted indexing and query tuning brought API latency down about 35% under production load.
r1.b2: Moved deployments to container-based CI/CD (Docker, ECR, ECS via CodeBuild/CodePipeline), with Jest, Vitest, Pest, and PHPUnit suites gating each release. Deploy time went from roughly 20 minutes to under 5.
r1.b3: Designed and built a serverless support chatbot on Amazon Lex and AWS Lambda (Python) with a Twilio channel. It answers routine questions and hands off to a human agent when confidence drops, which cut the support team's manual triage.
r1.b4: Built a request-and-bid marketplace flow with escalation handling and an in-app Paymob wallet, so users can pay, get paid, and withdraw funds without leaving the platform.
r1.b5: Shipped bilingual (Arabic/English) live chat over Laravel Reverb WebSockets, voice and SMS through Twilio, FCM push notifications, and S3-backed media storage.
r1.b6: Built a NestJS rules engine for competition scoring and ranking on Prisma/PostgreSQL, plus live WebSocket leaderboards and Next.js operator dashboards and onboarding screens.
r1.b7: Set up a client's entire Azure side solo: infrastructure provisioning, API Management as the API gateway, and release pipelines in Azure DevOps.
r1.b8: Run AWS infrastructure (VPC, EC2, RDS, S3, CloudFront, IAM, Secrets Manager) for 5+ production environments, with CloudWatch dashboards, alarms, and structured logging.
r1.b9: Hardened API layers across products with Sanctum/JWT auth, RBAC, attribute-based routing, and self-validating DTOs. Bad requests get rejected before they reach business logic.

r2.summary: Government-sponsored intensive software engineering program (~1,200 hours).
r2.b1: Built full-stack apps on two backend ecosystems, Node.js/Express and Python (Django, Flask), with React frontends, secure REST APIs, auth flows, and role-based access control.
r2.b2: Modeled relational and NoSQL databases with normalization and indexing so queries stayed fast as data grew; containerized services with Docker and deployed them to AWS in Agile sprints.

r3.summary: Independent front-end work, mainly for e-commerce.
r3.b1: Built React storefront interfaces from design to production: responsive layouts, product catalog, and cart screens wired to REST APIs.
r3.b2: Set up a reusable component library with Context API state, which removed prop drilling and kept catalog and cart state consistent as product ranges grew.
r3.b3: Tuned rendering and asset loading to cut page load times and keep large product listings smooth.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.a1: Paula Magdy is a full-stack software engineer based in Cairo, Egypt, with 3+ years of experience across TypeScript (NestJS/Next.js), PHP (Laravel), and Python (Django/Flask) on AWS, Azure, and Huawei Cloud. An AWS Certified Solutions Architect, he builds production web platforms with cross-functional teams and is comfortable owning a feature from the data model to the deploy pipeline.
faq.q2: What technologies does Paula Magdy work with?
faq.a2: He builds with Next.js, React, and TypeScript on the frontend; Node.js, NestJS, and Express, plus Laravel (PHP) and Django/Flask (Python) on the backend; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, and Prisma ORM for data; and AWS, Azure, Huawei Cloud, Docker, and CI/CD for cloud and delivery.
faq.a3: At Challenge Group — an AWS/Huawei Cloud partner serving government and enterprise clients across Egypt, KSA, and the UAE — he has contributed to multiple production platforms as part of cross-functional Agile delivery teams. His work spans backend services for platforms serving 5,000+ concurrent users, transactional workflows including a request-and-bid marketplace and an in-app Paymob wallet, real-time chat and messaging, Next.js/React interfaces and role-based admin panels, AWS and Azure infrastructure with container-first CI/CD, and a serverless Amazon Lex support chatbot.
faq.q4: Where is Paula Magdy based, and is he open to remote work?
faq.a4: He is based in Cairo, Egypt, and is open to full-stack engineering roles and consulting engagements, including remote work.
faq.q5: What certifications does Paula Magdy hold?
faq.a5: He holds the AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) and AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner certifications, plus Huawei Cloud's HCCDP – Solution Architectures and HCCDA – Tech Essentials — alongside a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Information Systems from October 6 University.
faq.q6: How can I get in touch with Paula Magdy?
faq.a6: You can reach him by email at paulamagdy665@gmail.com or through the contact form on this site — he typically replies within 24 hours.
